title: Exact associated-sheaf comparison on a principal affine neighbourhood
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], K a derived module-sheaf object [def-pc-derived-category], s in an affine open U, and M any complex of A=Gamma(X,U)-modules. Suppose the associated-sheaf complex [lem-pc-affine-perfect-module-model] represents K on the over-site of U. If f is outside the prime corresponding to s, there are an open V containing s and an additive exact functor F from A_f-modules to module sheaves on V which sends every finite free A_f-module of rank m to the finite free structure-sheaf module of rank m, such that K restricted to V is isomorphic to Q(F applied termwise to A_f tensor_A M) [def-pc-ring-tensor-cohomology]. The assertion has no boundedness, flatness, perfection or splitting hypothesis.

proof.text: Let j:Spec(A_f)->Spec(A), compose with the inverse affine chart and U->X, and take V to be its open image. Since f is not in the prime of s, s lies in V. The open immersion induces e:Spec(A_f) isomorphic to V. Set F to tilde followed by restriction along e inverse.

source.place: Tags 01HV and 01IB, associated sheaf localization and affine equivalence

proof.text: Associated sheaf preserves finite limits, and its adjunction gives preservation of colimits. Restriction along an open immersion is exact. Their composite F is additive and exact. Tilde of a finite free module is finite free; restriction preserves this identification.

source.place: Tags 01HV and 01IB, associated sheaf localization and affine equivalence

proof.text: Factor V->X through U. The over-site equivalences and restriction composition identify restriction to V of the original sheafification with tilde_A followed by restriction along Spec(A_f)->Spec(A) and e inverse. The natural tilde-pullback isomorphism identifies this with extension of scalars A->A_f followed by F. Apply this isomorphism termwise, pass to derived categories using exactness, and compose with the supplied model isomorphism.

theorem affine_principal_model_comparison (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ U : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    [∀ U : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))]
    (K : schemeDerivedCategory X) (s : X)
    (U : X.Opens) (hsU : s ∈ U) (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
    (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} (X.presheaf.obj (.op U))) ℤ)
    (eM : Nonempty ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
      (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj K ≅
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (((Scheme.affinePerfectSheafification X U hU).mapHomologicalComplex
            (.up ℤ)).obj M)))
    (f : X.presheaf.obj (.op U)) (hf : f ∉ (hU.isoSpec.hom ⟨s, hsU⟩).asIdeal) :
    ∃ V : X.Opens, s ∈ V ∧
      ∃ F : ModuleCat.{u} (Localization.Away f) ⥤
        SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings V.toScheme.toRingedSpace),
        ∃ hF : F.Additive, PreservesFiniteLimits F ∧ PreservesFiniteColimits F ∧
        (∀ m : ℕ, Nonempty (F.obj
          (ModuleCat.of (Localization.Away f) (ULift.{u} (Fin m) →₀ Localization.Away f)) ≅
          SheafOfModules.free (R := moduleRings V.toScheme.toRingedSpace)
            (ULift.{u} (Fin m)))) ∧
        letI : F.Additive := hF
        Nonempty
          (((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) V) ⋙
            Equivalence.functor
              (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V))
              (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings V.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
              (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv V)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K ≅
            DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
              ((RingTensorCohomology.extend _ (Localization.Away f)).obj M)))
